title: SYSK Selects: How much money is there in the world?​
summary: A Stuff You Should Know Selects rerun (originally aired September 2013) in which Josh and Chuck explore how much money exists in the world. They explain the Federal Reserve's money supply measures (M0, M1, M2, and the dropped M3), estimate that about $1.2 trillion in US cash circulates with roughly half to two-thirds held overseas, and discuss how money is tracked and why global totals are hard to estimate. They cover Zimbabwe's hyperinflation and its abandonment of the Zim dollar, and debate a universal world currency, its pros and cons, past attempts, and regional currency unions. The episode closes with listener mail and a thank-you segment for listener gifts.

segments.title: Selects intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces this Selects episode, first aired September 2013, and banters with Chuck about how much cash they carry.

segments.title: US dollars in the world and the M0 money supply
segments.summary: The hosts define the M0 money supply as all physical bills and coins, about $1.2 trillion in US dollars as of July 2013, which works out to roughly $3,800 per American if divided evenly. About half to two-thirds is held overseas.

segments.title: M1 and M2 money supply measures
segments.summary: M1 adds checking and travelers checks to M0, at about $2.5 trillion. M2 adds money market funds, savings accounts, and small CDs, at about $10.5 trillion. The Fed dropped M3 in 2006.

segments.title: Zimbabwe hyperinflation
segments.summary: Zimbabwe's money printing led to hyperinflation, with toilet paper prices soaring and prices doubling roughly every day. Annual inflation reached extreme levels, and in 2009 the government allowed foreign currencies, abandoning the Zim dollar. Very large denominations were printed, and the notes now sell as collectibles.

segments.title: Why global money is hard to track
segments.summary: Not every country has a central bank like the Fed, and Zimbabwe never tracked its printing. Economist Katherine Whitbourne reported that a blogger's last estimate of global money was about $5 trillion in M0 and $55 trillion in M2, as of about 2010.

segments.title: Universal world currency: pros, cons, and history
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a single world currency, citing Keynes, historic empires that shared currencies, and the post-WWII attempt that failed over pound versus dollar. Pros include no conversion fees and less speculation. Cons include who would run it and the loss of national tools like devaluation. They mention the gold standard debate and regional unions: the West and Central African CFA francs, Latin American and North American Union (Amero) proposals.

segments.title: Listener mail and thank-yous
segments.summary: The hosts read listener mail and thank listeners for books, postcards, music CDs, vinyl, and other gifts, then give contact information.
